gloss_en: sukkah — the covered festival booth (the mitzvah-structure of Sukkot), understood as a sheltering canopy/covering (root ס-כ-ך, 'to screen over'), which Rabbi Nachman identifies with Binah ('mother who covers her children'), chesed/embrace, the shade of the divine hand, encompassing lights (makifim), and divine effluence — not the verb סָכָה 'to gaze/see' (though homiletically linked to it), nor any other same-lettered word
